note: Documents that a human runs by hand and that no CI job reaches, on purpose (issue #237), and targets whose `##` help line claims CI coverage that no CI job delivers (issue #239). `make check-wiring` fails when a document is named only by a target CI never calls and no entry here records why — an omission has to be a dated decision, not an accident. An entry that CI starts reaching is STALE and must be deleted, so this file cannot rot either. A target entry records a help line that was corrected instead of wired: it is stale the moment CI starts reaching it.

tests/test_health.py.reason: The INSTALLED launcher serves the 0.5B model on this host's real backend (Metal on an Apple-Silicon Mac, the host docker on Linux) — hardware, not a gate. A CI runner has neither, and the cpu-health stage answers "hi" through the engine image instead (make test-health).

tests/test_native_engine_real.py.reason: Native Metal engines (issue #114) run only on an Apple-Silicon host: a CI runner has no Metal GPU and every Linux engine is tested inside its own image. The macOS pipeline runs the non-Metal half.

tests/test_native_engine_light.py.reason: Same Metal-only scope as test_native_engine_real.py: it serves the lightest TensorFold model through the native start script, or proves the budget refusal on a host too small for it — both need real Metal.

tests/test_interactive_tensorfold_real.p.reason: The interactive pty pick with a REAL native install and Metal serve (issue #114). Metal-only; the macOS runner variant (make test-interactive-tensorfold-ci, --dry) is the CI-adjacent form and the real serve stays a human-run check.

tests/test_install_published.py.reason: The published-install consumer test (pull a backend's published images, install + dl/uninstall). With issue #1027 the engine install/serve test lives in the engine-build producer (make test-engine-install per row on the just-published image) and ci.yml's install row is PRODUCT-ONLY, so no CI job reaches make test-install-published any more — it stays a human/host target.

tests/test_install_trend.py.reason: Host-only install-trend consumer test: `make test-install-trend` installs a trending top-tier model on a real host (network + disk); no CI job reaches it. Engine install/serve lives in the engine-build producer (#1027); this stays a human/host check.

agent-image-pull.reason: Convenience wrapper for a human: pull the published agent image and fail loudly when it is not there. No CI job calls it — publish-agent-image.yml PUSHES and reaches GHCR through scripts/ci_images.py directly — and its help line no longer claims otherwise. Kept because 'pull back what was published' is exactly what a human needs after a failed publish.
